newsitem.title: ITALY: Any EMU start uncertainty will hurt Italy - Bersani.
newsitem.headline: Any EMU start uncertainty will hurt Italy - Bersani.

text.p: Italian Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani said any uncertainty over the planned start of the single European currency would hurt Italy which has made greater efforts to make the grade than other European partners.

Italy had a "clear position" over the EMU timetable and was making its "contribution to the stability of the single currency. "We know that any uncertainty would damage us," he told reporters attending the annual meeting of the Lombardy region industrialists' association Assolombarda.
He urged European partners to confirm dates and parameters, even if more discussion of the subject would be desirable.
"We should try to give a political perspective to this Europe and start working out programmes paying close attention to employment. A real and proper jobs programme is needed," he added.
The minister underlined Italian efforts to overhaul state finances to meet the January 1, 1999 deadline.
European Union finance ministers are meeting today in Luxembourg for talks likely to be dominated by concerns over the new French government's views on aspects of the single currency.
He said he hoped the EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17 would be the occasion to reflect on the state of Italian economic recovery.
He did not elaborate but earlier told reporters that he saw the Italian economy making only a gradual recovery in the second half of this year.
He said he saw some "not very forceful signs of growth in the second half but a rather gradual trend towards recovery."

Italy will probably present its EMU convergence plan to the European Commission before the Amsterdam summit even if the final version will only be ready around June 20 so it can be discussed by a EU monetary committee on June 25, according to sources in the Italian delegation attending the Luxembourg Ecofin meeting.
The plan, based on the Italian government's 1998-2000 economic target document known as the DPEF, is expected to be approved definitively at the next Ecofin meeting set for July 7.
